en.question: A Governor General usually serves a term of ten years.
en.explanation: False. A Governor General usually serves for five years, not ten.

source.excerpt: The Sovereign is represented in Canada by the Governor General, who is appointed by the Sovereign on the advice of the Prime Minister, usually for five years.

fr.question: Un gouverneur général occupe habituellement ses fonctions pendant dix ans.
fr.explanation: Faux. Un gouverneur général occupe habituellement ses fonctions pendant cinq ans, et non dix.

source.chapter: Les Canadiens et leur système de gouvernement
source.excerpt: Le souverain est représenté au Canada par le gouverneur général, qui est nommé par le souverain sur recommandation du premier ministre, habituellement pour cinq ans.

en.question: A Lieutenant Governor represents the Sovereign in each of the three territories.
en.explanation: False. A Lieutenant Governor represents the Sovereign in each of the ten provinces, not the three territories — a Commissioner represents the federal government in the territories.

source.excerpt: In each of the ten provinces, the Sovereign is represented by the Lieutenant Governor, who is appointed by the Governor General on the advice of the Prime Minister, also usually for five years.

fr.question: Un lieutenant-gouverneur représente le souverain dans chacun des trois territoires.
fr.explanation: Faux. Un lieutenant-gouverneur représente le souverain dans chacune des dix provinces, et non dans les trois territoires — c'est un commissaire qui représente le gouvernement fédéral dans les territoires.

source.chapter: Les Canadiens et leur système de gouvernement
source.excerpt: Dans chacune des dix provinces, le souverain est représenté par le lieutenant-gouverneur, qui est nommé par le gouverneur général sur recommandation du premier ministre, aussi habituellement pour cinq ans.

en.question: Before a bill can become law in Canada, it must pass both Houses and receive what?
en.explanation: A bill must receive Royal Assent to become law.

source.excerpt: No bill may become law in Canada until it has passed both Houses and has received Royal Assent, granted by the Governor General on behalf of the Sovereign.

fr.question: Avant qu'un projet de loi ne devienne loi au Canada, il doit être adopté par les deux Chambres et obtenir quoi ?
fr.explanation: Un projet de loi doit obtenir la sanction royale pour devenir loi.

en.question: Cabinet ministers are accountable to elected representatives, meaning they must retain what?
options: The support of the Senate only
en.explanation: Cabinet ministers must retain the confidence of the House.

en.question: Who appoints Senators, and until what age do they serve?
options: The Governor General, on the advice of the Prime Minister, until age 75
Voters elect them directly, for a 6-year term
The Prime Minister appoints them for life
The provincial legislatures appoint them until age 65
en.explanation: Senators are appointed by the Governor General on the advice of the Prime Minister and serve until age 75.

source.excerpt: Senators are appointed by the Governor General on the advice of the Prime Minister and serve until age 75.

fr.question: Qui nomme les sénateurs, et jusqu'à quel âge restent-ils en poste ?
options: Le gouverneur général, sur recommandation du premier ministre, jusqu'à 75 ans
Les électeurs les élisent directement, pour un mandat de 6 ans
Le premier ministre les nomme à vie
Les assemblées législatives provinciales les nomment jusqu'à 65 ans
fr.explanation: Les sénateurs sont nommés par le gouverneur général et restent en poste jusqu'à l'âge de 75 ans.

source.chapter: Les Canadiens et leur système de gouvernement
source.excerpt: Les sénateurs sont nommés par le gouverneur général sur recommandation du premier ministre et restent en poste jusqu'à l'âge de 75 ans.

ar.question: من يُعيّن أعضاء مجلس الشيوخ، وحتى أي عمر يخدمون؟
options: الحاكم العام، بناءً على مشورة رئيس الوزراء، حتى سن 75
ينتخبهم الناخبون مباشرةً لولاية مدتها 6 سنوات
تُعيّنهم المجالس التشريعية الإقليمية حتى سن 65
ar.explanation: يُعيَّن أعضاء مجلس الشيوخ من قبل الحاكم العام بناءً على مشورة رئيس الوزراء ويخدمون حتى سن 75.

en.question: Who appoints the Governor General, and on whose advice?
options: The Sovereign, on the advice of the Prime Minister
The House of Commons, by majority vote
The Senate, on the advice of the Chief Justice
en.explanation: The Governor General is appointed by the Sovereign on the advice of the Prime Minister.

source.excerpt: The Sovereign is represented in Canada by the Governor General, who is appointed by the Sovereign on the advice of the Prime Minister, usually for five years.

fr.question: Qui nomme le gouverneur général, et sur quelle recommandation ?
options: Le souverain, sur recommandation du premier ministre
La Chambre des communes, par vote majoritaire
Le Sénat, sur recommandation du juge en chef
Les premiers ministres provinciaux, par consensus
fr.explanation: Le gouverneur général est nommé par le souverain sur recommandation du premier ministre.

source.chapter: Les Canadiens et leur système de gouvernement
source.excerpt: Le souverain est représenté au Canada par le gouverneur général, qui est nommé par le souverain sur recommandation du premier ministre, habituellement pour cinq ans.

ar.question: من يُعيّن الحاكم العام، وبناءً على مشورة من؟
options: السيادة (الملك)، بناءً على مشورة رئيس الوزراء
مجلس الشيوخ، بناءً على مشورة رئيس القضاة
ar.explanation: يُعيَّن الحاكم العام من قبل السيادة (الملك) بناءً على مشورة رئيس الوزراء.

en.question: Who can question Cabinet decisions in Canada?
options: All members of the House of Commons
en.explanation: Page 63: 'Their decisions can be questioned by all members of the House of Commons.' This is the role of Question Period.

optionAnnotations.explanation: Page 63: 'Their decisions can be questioned by all members of the House of Commons.' This is the role of Question Period.
The elected House of Commons holds the government accountable, not the Sovereign personally.
Opposition is most active in questioning, but ALL MPs (including government backbenchers) can question per p. 63.
The Senate reviews bills (p. 55) but the House of Commons is where the government is daily held accountable.

en.question: Who chooses the federal Cabinet ministers in Canada?
options: The Prime Minister, most of them from among members of the House of Commons
Canadian voters elect Cabinet ministers directly
The Governor General, on the advice of the Sovereign
en.explanation: Page 63: 'The Prime Minister chooses the ministers of the Crown, most of them from among members of the House of Commons. Cabinet ministers are responsible for running the federal government departments.'

optionAnnotations.explanation: Page 63: 'The Prime Minister chooses the ministers of the Crown, most of them from among members of the House of Commons. Cabinet ministers are responsible for running the federal government departments.'
Voters elect MPs to the House of Commons; the PM then chooses who in the elected caucus becomes a Cabinet minister.
The Governor General formally appoints Cabinet, but only on the PRIME MINISTER's recommendation (p. 63). The active choice is the PM's.
The Senate reviews legislation (p. 55) but does not pick Cabinet ministers.

en.question: Who is Canada's Head of Government, actually running the country, as distinct from the Head of State?
en.explanation: The Prime Minister is Head of Government and actually runs the country.

source.excerpt: There is a clear distinction in Canada between the Head of State — the Sovereign — and the Head of Government — the Prime Minister, who actually runs the country.

fr.question: Qui est le chef du gouvernement du Canada, celui qui dirige réellement le pays, par opposition au chef d'État ?
fr.explanation: Le premier ministre est le chef du gouvernement et dirige réellement le pays.

source.chapter: Les Canadiens et leur système de gouvernement
source.excerpt: Il existe une nette distinction au Canada entre le chef d'État — le souverain — et le chef du gouvernement — le premier ministre, qui dirige réellement le pays.

ar.question: من هو رئيس حكومة كندا، الذي يدير البلاد فعليًا، تمييزًا عن رئيس الدولة؟
ar.explanation: رئيس الوزراء هو رئيس الحكومة ويدير البلاد فعليًا.

en.question: Who is Canada's Head of State, as distinct from the Head of Government?
en.explanation: The Sovereign is Canada's Head of State.

source.excerpt: There is a clear distinction in Canada between the Head of State — the Sovereign — and the Head of Government — the Prime Minister, who actually runs the country.

fr.question: Qui est le chef d'État du Canada, par opposition au chef du gouvernement ?
fr.explanation: Le souverain est le chef d'État du Canada.

source.chapter: Les Canadiens et leur système de gouvernement
source.excerpt: Il existe une nette distinction au Canada entre le chef d'État — le souverain — et le chef du gouvernement — le premier ministre, qui dirige réellement le pays.

ar.question: من هو رئيس دولة كندا، تمييزًا عن رئيس الحكومة؟
ar.explanation: السيادة (الملك) هو رئيس دولة كندا.

en.question: Who leads First Nations governments on reserves?
en.explanation: Page 69: 'The First Nations have band chiefs and councillors who have major responsibilities on First Nations reserves, including housing, schools and other services.'

optionAnnotations.explanation: Page 69: 'The First Nations have band chiefs and councillors who have major responsibilities on First Nations reserves, including housing, schools and other services.'
Premiers head provincial governments (p. 58), not band councils.
Mayors and councillors lead municipalities (p. 66), not First Nations reserves.
Senators are appointed federal legislators (p. 55), not band leaders.

en.question: Who prepares the federal budget?
en.explanation: Page 63: 'They [Cabinet] prepare the budget and propose most new laws.'

optionAnnotations.explanation: Page 63: 'They [Cabinet] prepare the budget and propose most new laws.'
The Senate reviews but doesn't prepare budgets.
Premiers prepare PROVINCIAL budgets, not federal.
The Bank of Canada manages monetary policy (p. 42), not budgets.

en.question: Who proposes most new federal laws?
en.explanation: Page 63: 'They [Cabinet] prepare the budget and propose most new laws.' Opposition MPs and individual government MPs can also introduce private members' bills, but most laws originate with Cabinet.

optionAnnotations.explanation: Page 63: 'They [Cabinet] prepare the budget and propose most new laws.' Opposition MPs and individual government MPs can also introduce private members' bills, but most laws originate with Cabinet.
The Senate reviews bills (p. 55) but most originate with Cabinet.
Federal laws come from the federal Cabinet.
Canada does not have national citizen-initiative legislation.

en.question: Who represents the Sovereign in Canada at the federal level, and how is this person appointed?
options: The Governor General, appointed by the Sovereign on the advice of the Prime Minister, usually for five years
The Prime Minister, elected by the people for four years
The Lieutenant Governor, appointed by the federal Cabinet
The Senate Speaker, elected by senators
en.explanation: Page 57: 'The Sovereign is represented in Canada by the Governor General, who is appointed by the Sovereign on the advice of the Prime Minister, usually for five years.'

optionAnnotations.explanation: Page 57: 'The Sovereign is represented in Canada by the Governor General, who is appointed by the Sovereign on the advice of the Prime Minister, usually for five years.'
The PM is head of government, not the Sovereign's representative. The PM is also not directly elected — the leader of the party with the most seats forms the government (p. 62).
The Lieutenant Governor represents the Sovereign at the PROVINCIAL level, not federal — and is appointed by the Governor General on the PM's advice (p. 57).
The Senate Speaker is a parliamentary role, not the Sovereign's representative.
